title: Annotated Speech Corpus for Low Resource Indian Languages: Awadhi, Bhojpuri, Braj and Magahi
authors: Ritesh Kumar; Siddharth Singh; Shyam Ratan; Mohit Raj; Sonal Sinha; Sumitra Mishra; Bornini Lahiri; Vivek Seshadri; Kalika Bali; Atul Kr. Ojha
venue: 1st Workshop on Speech for Social Good (S4SG)
speech_type: Translated Hindi elicitation sentences and lifecycle narration prompts
base_model: Google Hindi STT; Azure Hindi STT; Kaldi mono/tri models; wav2vec-large-xlsr-53
training_method: Hindi STT baselines; monolingual/multilingual Kaldi; transfer learning with multilingual dataset
main_result: Awadhi WER: Google Hindi 79.9; Azure Hindi 83.2; Kaldi mono 86.3; tri1 80.9; tri2b 82.1; tri3b 82.5; wav2vec transfer row reports Awadhi as '-' while multilingual avg is 40.4
relevance_to_our_project: Establishes existing Indian Awadhi speech corpus and ASR baselines; weakens any first Awadhi ASR/corpus claim
overlap_with_our_proposal: Directly overlaps Awadhi corpus and low-resource Awadhi ASR portions
remaining_gap: Nepal-Awadhi not included; cross-border India/Nepal generalization not tested; Hindi vs Nepali donor comparison not tested
verification_notes: Verified via ISCA page and PDF. Speaker region for Awadhi is Pratapgarh Uttar Pradesh; no Nepal-Awadhi reported. Wav2vec Awadhi cell appears missing/dash in Table 4 so do not infer an Awadhi-specific wav2vec WER.

title: Dialect Matters: Cross-Lingual ASR Transfer for Low-Resource Indic Language Varieties
authors: Akriti Dhasmana; Aarohi Srivastava; David Chiang
peer_review_status: Accepted at VarDial 2026; arXiv version inspected
languages: Devanagari-script Indic varieties in VAANI including Awadhi; Garhwali case study
dataset_hours: UNKNOWN for Awadhi in inspected text; cross-lingual experiments use 1-7 hours per fine-tuning language depending on availability; test samples up to 1 hour
base_model: IndicWav2Vec-Hindi; w2vBERT; Wav2Vec2; HuBERT; XLS-R; Whisper-small for Garhwali case study
training_method: Zero-shot evaluation; cross-lingual fine-tuning; Garhwali model comparison
donor_languages: Multiple VAANI-D donor languages including Hindi; donor-target matrix includes Awadhi as target/evaluation variety
main_result: For Awadhi target in donor comparison table: DonorRank/genetic donor hne gives CER 22.4 and WER 55.0; Hindi baseline gives CER 34.3 and WER 81.2
relevance_to_our_project: Highly relevant for dialectal transfer, Awadhi in VAANI, bias toward Hindi, and spontaneous/code-mixed evaluation
overlap_with_our_proposal: Strong overlap with donor-language transfer and dominant-language normalization/error-analysis concepts
remaining_gap: Nepal-Awadhi not included; Nepali donor not central for Awadhi; no India-vs-Nepal Awadhi comparison
verification_notes: Verified via arXiv abstract page and HTML full text. VAANI described as India-wide dataset; no Nepal-Awadhi evidence found in paper.

title: DonorRank: Donor Language Selection for Low-Resource Cross-Lingual Speech Recognition
authors: Akriti Dhasmana; Aarohi Srivastava; David Chiang
languages: VAANI-D Indic varieties and WAXAL African languages
dataset_hours: VAANI-D uses max seven donor training hours and one hour test per language; full VAANI described as over 150000 hours with about 10 percent transcribed
speech_type: Spontaneous speech; VAANI-D image-description speech; WAXAL spontaneous speech
training_method: Single-donor zero-shot transfer; learning-to-rank donor prediction; multi-donor transfer
donor_languages: Multiple; for Awadhi target top donor reported as hne; Hindi is high-resource baseline
main_result: For VAANI-D Awadhi target: DonorRank top donor hne CER 22.4/WER 55.0 versus Hindi CER 34.3/WER 81.2; multi-donor experiments include Awadhi among six primary targets
relevance_to_our_project: Directly relevant to donor-language selection involving Awadhi and multi-donor transfer
overlap_with_our_proposal: High overlap with donor selection and target Awadhi transfer framing
remaining_gap: No Nepal-Awadhi; no Hindi vs Nepali donor comparison for Nepal-Awadhi; preprint status; donor code hne needs exact language expansion verified
verification_notes: Verified via arXiv page and HTML full text. Treat as preprint unless later venue appears.

title: Nwāchā Munā: A Devanagari Speech Corpus and Proximal Transfer Benchmark for Nepal Bhasha ASR
authors: Rishikesh Kumar Sharma; Safal Narshing Shrestha; Jenny Poudel; Rupak Tiwari; Arju Shrestha; Rupak Raj Ghimire; Bal Krishna Bal
peer_review_status: Accepted in CHiPSAL@LREC 2026; arXiv version inspected
dataset_hours: 5.39 hours labelled; 9.33 hours pseudo-labelled after filtering; 23.05 augmented hours in one condition
speech_type: Mostly read/formal sentences; supplemented by about one hour web audio; spontaneous coverage limited
training_method: Zero-shot NepConformer; supervised fine-tuning; decoder-only fine-tuning; shallow fusion; augmentation; semi-supervised learning
main_result: Best reported CER 17.59 for NepConformer with augmented data; zero-shot NepConformer CER 52.54; Whisper-Small fine-tuned base data CER 18.76
relevance_to_our_project: Relevant Nepal-language proximal transfer analogue and warning about speaker splits and text normalization
overlap_with_our_proposal: Methodological overlap with Nepali donor transfer and small-corpus ASR in Nepal
remaining_gap: Not Awadhi; not Nepal-Awadhi; no Hindi-vs-Nepali donor comparison; speaker-disjoint split not enforced
verification_notes: Verified via arXiv page and HTML full text. The paper explicitly maintains speaker representation in all splits rather than strict speaker independence.

title: Speech-to-Speech Machine Translation for Dialectal Variations of Hindi
authors: Sanmay Sood; Siddharth Rajput; Md Shad Akhtar
venue: Proceedings of the Twelfth Workshop on Asian Translation (WAT 2025)
languages: Awadhi; Bhojpuri; Braj Bhasha; Magahi; Hindi; English
dataset_hours: SpeeD-IA parallel subset 267 sentences; VAANI sampled about 4-5 hours per target dialect and 18 hours total
speech_type: SpeeD-IA spoken translations; VAANI monolingual audio; lifecycle narrations
training_method: Whisper fine-tuning; Google STT zero-shot baseline; cascaded ASR-MT-TTS
evaluation_metrics: WER for ASR; BLEU/COMET/BLEURT for MT; MOS for TTS/S2ST
main_result: ASR Table 12: Awadhi WER Google STT 0.7321; fine-tuned Whisper-Medium 0.4542
relevance_to_our_project: Shows 2025 Awadhi speech technology and Whisper fine-tuning; weakens any claim that Whisper adaptation for Awadhi is unstudied
overlap_with_our_proposal: Overlaps practical ASR baseline and downstream speech-to-speech pipeline for Awadhi/Bhojpuri/Braj/Magahi
remaining_gap: Nepal-Awadhi only mentioned via general linguistic appendix based on non-primary references; no Nepal-Awadhi ASR or cross-border evaluation
verification_notes: Verified via ACL Anthology page and PDF. Treat Appendix statements on Awadhi geography cautiously because they cite Wikipedia rather than a linguistic primary source.
